questions.text: What happens inside you when you imagine setting down the invisible weight of always caring for everyone else?
Where does the quiet residue of your anger go when you finally allow yourself to speak it out loud?
How do you hold love for someone who is slowly slipping away while still honoring your own presence in the room?
What stories have you carried about what might shatter if your voice were to suddenly take up space?
What would your body whisper to you if it no longer had to earn the right to rest?
What new version of yourself emerges when an entire afternoon belongs to no one else but you?
What changes in your chest when you realize you do not have to carry your heaviest memories completely alone?
How does it feel to look right at your own truth without needing to disguise the hardest parts?
